mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate environment consistently compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 2.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals labor market slack and economic weakness, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in industrial production and housing starts signal robust economic demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60-day horizons when INDPRO > 100 and HOUST > 1300.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO > 100 and HOUST > 1300 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 250), central banks tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 250 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth consistently correlates with positive equity returns, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20-day horizons when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1300 thousand units signal weak consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1300 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment and decreases in the federal funds rate signal accommodative monetary policy and strong labor markets, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.1% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In industrial contraction regimes (INDPRO < 100), manufacturing weakness reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 over any 3-year rolling window.
